Consult Summary:
- Adult male presents with acute onset watery diarrhea, left lower abdominal cramps, and associated symptoms following recent takeaway food; assessment consistent with gastroenteritis, conservative management advised.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Diarrhea for three days, impacting daily activities, requiring proximity to toilet.
- Timeline: Symptoms began three days ago; vomiting occurred at onset, now resolved; felt feverish at start but currently afebrile.
- Symptom details:
  - Stool frequency: 6–7 times per day, watery and loose.
  - Abdominal pain: Cramp-like, intermittent, localized to left lower abdomen.
  - Associated symptoms: Initial vomiting (now resolved), felt weak and shaky, transient feverish feeling at symptom onset, persistent loss of appetite but able to tolerate fluids and light foods.
  - Denies blood in stool or vomit.
  - No ongoing fever, no night sweats, no current vomiting.
  - Systems review: No other bowel or abdominal complaints reported; able to maintain hydration with fluids and light food.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: None specified.
- Trigger: Ate Chinese takeaway four days ago; no significant dietary changes otherwise.
- Possible exposure: One child had vomiting but no diarrhea; no other household members affected.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma, well-controlled; uses inhaler (medication name/type/dose/route/frequency not documented).
- No other chronic illnesses reported.
- No other medications taken.

Social History:
- Occupation: Accountant; continued working despite illness, finds symptoms disruptive.
- Lives with wife and two children.
- Smoking: Denies use.
- Alcohol: Denies use.

Family History:
- Wife and two children; one child recently vomited without diarrhea.
- No other family medical history mentioned.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed/documented during consult.

Investigations:
- None performed at this time.
- Doctor mentioned possible stool testing if symptoms persist beyond 3–4 days.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Gastroenteritis (likely viral, possible bacterial etiology)
  - Advise conservative management.
  - Emphasize maintaining hydration with fluids and oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte).
  - Use paracetamol (acetaminophen) for symptom relief as needed: 2 tablets up to four times a day (dose/strength not documented).
  - Recommend rest and time off work for 2–3 days.
  - Advise to monitor symptoms and seek review if not improved after 3–4 days or if new concerning symptoms develop.
  - Consider stool sample and further investigations if symptoms persist.
- General plan items:
  - Patient education provided regarding expected course and red flags.

Quality checks:

●	Missing but clinically expected elements: Drug allergies not documented; vital signs not recorded; inhaler type and dosing not specified; full family history and systems review not completed; no physical exam findings; medication reconciliation incomplete.
●	Internal conflicts: None identified.
●	Transcript quality: Clear, minimal background noise, all clinically relevant information captured.
